header.incumbent: Homegrown billing system, built by an employee who has since left
header.tag_why: A CFO freeze stopped the deal, but before it Owen said he couldn't get it past Diane "without a number that's ours"; we sent the generic ROI deck, never built that number, and never put a case in front of the person who decided.

evidence.excerpt: There wasn't one big thing.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Their VP of Product, Owen, had wanted to rebuild billing for a while.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The billing system is homegrown, built by a guy who left, and every pricing change takes them a quarter.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: He wanted it done before they launched a new pricing tier, but the tier didn't have a date either.
evidence.label: fact

trigger.insight: This was one product leader's long-held wish with no deadline and no event behind it. Nothing tied it to a date or to a cost finance could see, so a budget freeze could stop it with no friction. The real pain, a quarter for every pricing change, is a cost in engineering time, and nobody ever turned it into money.
trigger.messaging: When the buyer reaches out without a deadline, help them create one: tie the cost of a quarter-per-pricing-change to a named launch (the new tier) so the status quo has a visible price before finance looks at it.

evidence.excerpt: The CFO, I guess? Diane.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Owen told me. I never spoke to her.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: No. Owen said he'd bring her in at the end.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We only ever talked to product and engineering.
evidence.label: fact

decider.insight: Diane held the real veto, and the rep knew it only through Owen. Diane was in no meeting. Leaving her for the end meant the first thing finance saw from this deal was, at most, whatever Owen carried in. The transcript does not say whether Owen ever showed her anything. Calling it a freeze "against everything" hides the fact that we never gave finance a reason to exempt us.
decider.messaging: Build a finance-facing version of the billing pitch (cost of the homegrown system, payback period) and ask the champion to bring the CFO in before paper goes out, not "at the end".

evidence.excerpt: There wasn't one. It was us against doing nothing.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Owen never looked at anybody else, as far as I know.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Toward the end Owen started asking for things for finance.
evidence.label: fact

competitor.insight: The competitor was the status quo, plus a budget rule. The rep is not sure whether Owen looked at other vendors, and nobody asked whether rebuilding in-house was an option. The one real change in the questions was the move to finance asks, which signalled the deal was heading to a budget owner we had never met.
competitor.messaging: Against doing nothing, lead with the cost of keeping a homegrown billing system whose builder has left, not with features a rival lacks.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the billing demo. Changing a price in a few clicks, trials, proration.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: His engineers were into it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap."
evidence.label: quote

message.insight: The demo landed because it gave engineering time back. Our revenue-growth framing (M7) was rejected outright, not met with silence. The rep's first answer was that nothing got silence, which hides that the room was only product and engineering: the audience that never heard the pitch was finance.
message.messaging: For product-led billing buyers, swap M7's grow-revenue line for the customer's own framing: billing stops being a tax on the roadmap, and a pricing change takes minutes, not a quarter.

evidence.excerpt: I sent him the ROI deck. The general one, with the study.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: We were going to set up a session to build one. Then Q3 closed.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: About a month.
evidence.label: fact

decided.insight: The warning came about a month before the freeze email, when the champion said in plain words that the generic study (M6) would not get past the CFO. The session to build a Pikeview-specific number never happened in that month. Whether that number would have beaten a freeze on all vendors is unclear, but it contradicts the rep's view that nothing could have been done.
decided.messaging: Retire the generic economic-impact study as the answer to "show payback" and replace it with a fast, customer-specific payback build offered the moment finance questions start.

evidence.excerpt: The number. Their own. What the homegrown system costs them.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: he mentioned once that some landlord subscriptions lapse because the card fails and nobody chases it. We never added it up.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Moving the existing subscriptions over without asking landlords for their card details again, and whether they could do it in stages.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We had a doc for that. He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: The gap was proof, not product. We had the pieces for a cost case (engineering time, billing errors, lapsed landlord subscriptions that failed-payment recovery speaks to) and never added them up. On migration we offered a doc when he wanted a peer who had done it. The transcript does not say whether that reference was ever provided.
gaps.messaging: Pair M10 with a cost-of-status-quo worksheet that counts lapsed subscriptions from failed cards, and answer migration questions (no card re-collection, staged moves) with a reference customer, not just a doc.

evidence.excerpt: Owen's was "a tax on the roadmap."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Owen said finance saw it as a nice to have.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "we don't touch billing before renewal season."
evidence.label: quote

language.insight: Product's words ("tax on the roadmap") and finance's words ("if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded") never met. No one turned the roadmap tax into something finance would see as a fire. The engineering lead's renewal-season rule is a second timing gate the rep's "it'll come back next year" doesn't account for.
language.messaging: Use "a tax on the roadmap" with product buyers, and for finance translate it into a quantified cost so the project reads as on fire rather than "nice to have".

gaps.question: Did Owen ever present a business case or our proposal to Diane, and what did she see before the freeze?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee to ask Owen directly what, if anything, reached Diane about this project.

gaps.question: Did Pikeview consider other vendors or rebuilding billing in-house?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee to confirm with Owen whether any alternative was looked at, given her 'as far as I know' hedge.

gaps.question: Which part of our pitch got silence?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee what topics engineering or Owen let drop without follow-up, beyond the revenue framing Owen rejected.

gaps.question: Why wasn't the payback-building session scheduled in the month between Owen's ask and the freeze?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee what blocked scheduling the session and who on our side could have built the number.

gaps.question: Was Owen ever connected with a reference customer who had done a similar migration?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee whether a reference call was offered or arranged, and if not, why not.

gaps.question: When does the freeze lift, and when is renewal season relative to that?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee to get from Owen the conditions for lifting the vendor hold and the renewal-season dates, to test 'it'll come back next year'.

close.rep_takeaway: When the champion says "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours," that's the deal telling you where it will die. Treat it as the top priority: build their number with them that week and use it to get in front of the CFO, rather than sending the generic deck and waiting for the end.
